title: Spatial locality and line size
description: A loop over consecutive words, with short lines and with long lines.

steps.text: The trace loads sixteen consecutive words, `0x000` to `0x03C`, as a loop over an array would. Words are 4 bytes, and the lines of this cache are 8 bytes, so each line holds two words. A miss brings in the whole line.
With two words per line, how many of the sixteen loads will miss?
steps.explain: Eight. The first word of each line misses and brings in its neighbour, so the second word hits: one miss for every two loads.
steps.hint: A miss loads a whole line. How many words does a line hold?
Press Run in the transport bar. If the trace has already run, press Undo, then Run.

steps.text: Eight misses and eight hits: a hit rate of 50%. Every hit used a neighbour that a miss had already brought in. That is *spatial locality*: after a word, the next one is likely to be wanted.
Set Line size to 32 B. The cache will ask to reset; choose Reset and apply.
steps.hint: Line size is in the bar above the cache. Pick 32 B.

steps.text: With 32-byte lines, each line holds eight words. How many of the sixteen loads will miss now?
steps.explain: Two. The first load of each 32-byte line misses and the other seven words hit: the sixteen words fill two lines.
steps.hint: Sixteen words, eight to a line.
Press Run in the transport bar.

steps.text: Two misses, fourteen hits: 87.5%. Longer lines gave more neighbours per miss. The price is that the same 128 bytes now hold only 4 lines instead of 16, so a program that jumps around would find fewer different lines in the cache.
